additions: Enforcement layering per the Claude Code docs: deny rules in settings.json are evaluated regardless of what a PreToolUse hook returns; a blocking hook (exit 2) also beats allow rules. Read/Edit deny rules use gitignore syntax (`Read(./runs/*/holdout/**)`), cover the file tools plus recognised Bash file commands (cat/head/tail/sed/tee) and redirections, but not Python/Node scripts that open files; `Write(path)` rules are ignored (use `Edit(path)`); OS-level enforcement needs sandboxing. Hooks never fire for @-mentioned files. So the holdout seal needs a `Read(...)` deny rule plus the hook, and the untrusted-code rule is a guardrail only; the real protection is to keep third-party clones outside the working tree (as the scratchpad already does) and never `--add-dir` them.

`-p`/headless specifics that change the orchestration: background Bash defaults drop to 10 minutes when the prompt is passed as text; the run waits at most 10 idle minutes for background work (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS); `--permission-prompts none` denies anything that would prompt; `--bare` skips project hooks/skills/CLAUDE.md (and a non-bare `-p` run executes a repo's .claude/settings.json hooks even in an untrusted folder, which matters when auditing third-party repos); a Workflow launch in `-p` needs `Workflow` or `Workflow(<name>)` in allow rules.

Kepler-specific vetting a professional expects and the brief under-specifies: per-quarter channel rotation (KBONUS LIGHTCURVE_Q headers carry QUARTER, SEASON, MODULE, OUTPUT, CHANNEL, FLFRCSAP, CROWDSAP, NPIXSAP, PSFFRAC, PERTRATI, PERTSTD; APERTURE_Q masks are in the originating TPF frame, TPFORG in the primary header) so difference images and centroids must be done per season and the dilution model must use per-quarter FLFRCSAP/CROWDSAP; 29.4-min cadence (XPOSURE 1765.464 s) requires exposure-time integration (supersampling) in any transit fit; timing conventions BKJD = BJD - 2454833, BTJD = BJD - 2457000, so BTJD = BKJD - 2167 exactly; Kepler DR25 Robovetter-style tests (odd/even, secondary, model-shift/ghost, rolling-band 'Skye') and the KOI false-positive flags (koi_fpflag_nt/ss/co/ec in `cumulative`) and Kepler EB catalogue (Villanova; Kuber's provenance.json records villanova_home.html) belong in the ephemeris-match step.

LEO-Vetter is usable on Kepler for flux-level vetting (README: 'any source, including ... Kepler, K2, and TESS'); only its pixel-level (difference-image) vetting is TESS-only. Cite Kunimoto et al. 2025, AJ 170, 280. This closes the brief's open question 7 for the flux-level metrics.

TRICERATOPS 1.1.0 dependency markers decide the env: on Python >=3.13 it requires numpy>=2.1 and scipy>=1.14 (so it can share a modern stack), on <3.13 it pins numpy<2 and scipy<1.14; keep it in its own venv either way because pytransit==2.2 is pinned.

Checkpoint design lesson from Kuber's own code: the cache key must include a hash of the pipeline code and parameters, not an integer version (SEARCH_AUDIT.md: 'Cache filenames contain only TIC/mode/inversion ... otherwise old JSON is silently reused'); write results atomically (acquire.py writes `.tmp.npz` then `replace`); record RNG seeds; record which SNR statistic is quoted (eumemic `refine` BLS SNR vs astropy `depth_snr` vs TLS SDE) because the three are not interchangeable.

Secrets handling for publishing: never give the agent a Zenodo token (a `Bash(curl * -X POST *zenodo.org*)` deny only matches that spelling, and Python `requests` is invisible to Bash rules); keep the token in a file covered by a `Read(...)` deny rule and let the human run the publish.

Routine prompts must explicitly say to act on the `<routine-fire-payload>` block; the /fire endpoint requires `anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01`; in cloud sessions `gh pr` (GraphQL) is rejected by the GitHub proxy, so a sector-watcher routine should open PRs with `gh api` or push a branch and let the UI create the PR.

Workflow sizing: with the default `medium` size guideline Claude aims for <10 agents; set `workflowSizeGuideline` (or `/config workflowSizeGuideline=large`) and `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` explicitly; on 4 CPUs the effective concurrency is min(16, 4-2) = 2 agents.

The developer's repo already contains a working single-star pipeline (pipeline/run.py with BLS 1-60 d ~2.5 min and TLS 1-30 d ~5 min per light curve on 3 threads, per pipeline/README.md) plus batch_search.py, modal_app.py, triage.py, ephemeris_match.py and a prereg_poolA.json; the agentic layer should wrap these modules rather than the brief's hypothetical module names.
